findings.description: Checking `email.toLowerCase().includes('demo')` will false-positive on legitimate emails like 'demonstration@company.com' or 'democorp@example.org'. Use exact domain match: `email.toLowerCase().endsWith('@cinegen.demo')`.

If Supabase Auth password update succeeds but the users table update fails, the user can log in via Supabase but any direct database password checks will use the old hash. Either fail the entire operation if the table update fails, or remove the table update entirely and rely only on Supabase Auth.

The reset-password page has no logic to detect token expiry before submission. If the user lands on the page with an expired token, they won't know until they fill out the form and click submit. Check `supabase.auth.getUser()` on page load and show an error state immediately if the session is invalid.

The forgot-password API falls back to `http://localhost:3000` if NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is unset, but production deployments without this variable will send reset links pointing to localhost. Add a warning log or fail the request in production if the variable is missing.

The reset-password page validates 8+ chars, uppercase, and number. The API enforces the same. But nowhere is it validated whether this matches the password requirements enforced during registration. Confirm that register uses the same rules, or document why reset has stricter requirements.
